title: Every asyncRewake wake is labelled "Stop hook feedback", whatever event armed it
summary: A wake from a SessionStart asyncRewake hook reaches the model as 'Stop hook blocking error from command "SessionStart:startup"' under the heading 'Stop hook feedback'. The user-visible summary line says 'Stop hook feedback' too. Nothing is wrong and no Stop hook is involved — that string is the hardcoded default. The model reads it literally and will tell your user a stop hook did something, so set rewakeSummary and rewakeMessage to your own wording or the feature looks like an error.

body.problem: You arm a SessionStart hook with asyncRewake, it exits 2, and the wake lands. What the model receives is a user-role turn whose content begins '<task-notification><summary>Stop hook feedback</summary></task-notification>' followed by '<system-reminder>Stop hook blocking error from command "SessionStart:startup": <your text></system-reminder>'. The terminal shows the same 'Stop hook feedback' line next to a bullet. Two misreadings follow. First, debugging: you go looking for a misconfigured Stop hook that does not exist. Second, and worse in production, the model takes the wording at face value — in our runs it reported to the user that 'a stop hook said there is 1 unread DM' and, on seeing the word 'error', treated a routine notification as a fault to investigate.
steps: Set rewakeSummary on the hook to the one-line string you want the user to see in the terminal, replacing the 'Stop hook feedback' default.
Set rewakeMessage to the prefix the model should see, replacing the 'Stop hook blocking error from command ...' framing.
Phrase both as a notification, not a failure: the word 'error' in the default prefix is what pushes the model into diagnosing rather than acting.
Keep the hook's own stderr text self-describing, since it is appended after your prefix and is what the model actually acts on.

pitfalls.tried: Searching settings.json and the plugin for the Stop hook named in the message
pitfalls.whyFailed: There is no Stop hook. The command name in the message ('SessionStart:startup') already tells you the real source; only the surrounding label is wrong.

pitfalls.tried: Leaving the defaults because the mechanism works
pitfalls.whyFailed: It works, but the model narrates the default wording to the user, so a working notification reads as an internal error.

body.verification: Arm a SessionStart asyncRewake hook that writes a plain sentence to stderr and exits 2. After the wake, grep the session transcript for 'Stop hook blocking error from command' — it will name your SessionStart hook. Set rewakeSummary/rewakeMessage and confirm both the transcript and the terminal line change.
body.appliesWhen: Claude Code 2.1.302 (CLI), asyncRewake hooks on any event other than Stop
body.notAppliesWhen: Hooks that actually are registered on Stop, where the label is accurate
